name: Duneborne
description: Being part of a duneborne community means you’ve made a home among the shifting sands and arid climate of the desert. Each duneborne enclave develops specific methods of protecting themselves from the blazing sun, moving across the scorching sands, and acquiring and storing precious resources. Some duneborne travel their desert homes, maneuvering through the dunes herding livestock, while others cluster around oases, collaborating with one another to maintain and share a rare area of abundant resources.

Duneborne settlements are known for architecture that captures wind to cool their homes and irrigation systems that tap into underground reservoirs and tend to crops even amidst the harshest conditions. Many duneborne put added emphasis on familial bonds and the need for everyone to contribute to the well-being of the collective.
Duneborne are often adaptable, centered, collaborative, devoted, cheerful, and observant.
features: Oasis: During a short rest, you or an ally can reroll a die used for a downtime move and take the higher result.

name: Freeborne
description: Being part of a freeborne community means you’re from a collective that once lived under tyrannical rule but is now liberated. Though no two freeborne enclaves are the same, all are unified by the experience of fighting to preserve their culture while others tried to eradicate it. Whether due to their religion, resources, location, or culture, freeborne groups were once subjugated by another community. For some, this subjugation might have only recently ended; for others, even if their freedom has been long-won, the scars of tyranny can last, bonding together families and neighbors for decades or even generations. Many freeborne collectives unify in and rebuild the lands reclaimed from their oppressors or in a homeland they were taken from. Others see “home” as a collection of people who care for one another, no matter where they reside.

Many freeborne passionately celebrate their unique holidays, art, food, decor, and other customs, whether they’re enjoying long-held traditions or new practices born from liberation. Their past experiences often forge in them a fierce protectiveness of their community and an equally strong fervor to celebrate their culture.
Freeborne are often optimistic, guarded, courageous, joyful, subversive, and traumatized.
features: Unbound: Once per session when you roll with Fear, you can change it into a roll with Hope instead.

name: Frostborne
description: Being part of a frostborne community means you come from a place of snow and ice. Forged in bitter and unrelenting cold, frostborne communities are accustomed to surviving in the harshest conditions. The glaciers and tundras they call home usually lack wood, so these collectives use more readily available materials such as ice, stone, bone, and animal pelts to make shelter and conserve heat. They are adept at ensuring their supplies go a long way and that all their people have access to the essentials needed to survive.

As part of their systems of survival, many frostborne closely track weather patterns, the rising and setting of the sun, and the needs of local flora and fauna. Because of the howling wind and biting snow, some frostborne communities develop nonverbal means of communication so they can cover their faces for safety during dangerous weather.
Frostborne are often cunning, gregarious, intrepid, purposeful, quiet, and warm.
features: Hardy: When you take a rest, you clear a Hit Point.

name: Hearthborne
description: Being part of a hearthborne community means you come from humble origins, having lived in a modest village or quaint countryside. These communities are often small groups that live in resource-rich, peaceful areas that allow families and neighbors the time to develop close-knit relationships rather than compete over scarce supplies. Hearthborne communities are largely agrarian and pastoral, focusing the layout of their villages around their plants and animals. The town centers typically feature a collection of locally owned shops with skilled artisans such as blacksmiths, cobblers, alchemists, and the like.

Sometimes, hearthborne communities have distant but powerful rulers who own the land the villagers work and live on—in those cases, resources are controlled by the wealthy even though the labor is performed by locals, and workers might struggle to afford the basics they need to survive. While some hearthborne individuals can be mistrustful of outsiders, most are known for being welcoming, peaceful, and hospitable.
Hearthborne are often careful, generous, insular, loquacious, smiley, and traditional.
features: Close-Knit: Once per long rest, you can **spend any number of Hope** to grant an ally within Far range an equal number of Hope.

name: Reborne
description: You were once a member of a different community that you’re no longer part of. Unlike members of collectives who are allied by familiarity, shared location, history, and culture, reborne are individuals who might never meet and are unified only by their shared experience of solitude. Whether they left by choice or were ripped from their community, all reborne are disconnected from the place where they once belonged, and they carry that wound with them.

Some reborne are isolated from their community because they chose to reject or renounce it, or they could have been forcibly expelled by other members. These instances are often due to a conflict, such as clashing ideological differences, a falling out with their people, or an incident that forced them to depart. Other reborne have no knowledge of their culture, either due to their upbringing or perhaps because they lost their memory through injury or magic. Some have even returned from beyond the veil after death with no recollection of their previous life—or the culture that shaped it.

Often, reborne individuals tirelessly search for their past or feel that they’ll never belong in a collective, but all are afforded the opportunity to turn toward the future and redefine themselves while building new bonds with those they come to know and love.
Reborne are often curious, hopeful, innocent, isolated, mournful, and uncanny.
features:
Found Family: Once per rest, you can **spend a Hope** to use an ally's Experience as if it were your own. When you do so, describe how your time with that ally prepared you for this moment.

When you join a new community or rediscover your old one, you can permanently trade this card for that one instead.

name: Warborne
description: Being part of a warborne community means you come from a place that is, or was, ravaged by war. These groups might be composed of civilians who live in an active warzone, soldiers who served together in the armed forces, or citizens of nations that have been in conflict for decades. Whether civilian or military, warborne are typically skilled in self-defense, even if their tactics are focused on avoidance rather than offensive action.

Warborne defending their homeland are known for using their environment to their advantage, while invading warborne might rely entirely on their military might. No matter their origin, the life of a warborne is defined at least in part by resourcefulness. Those who live in an occupied territory might need to undertake massive reconstruction efforts to repair and preserve homes, farms, workplaces, or cultural monuments— the remnants of one building often become the materials to repair another. Meanwhile, warborne who are part of an invading army typically carry few personal possessions and must rely on scavenging the warzones they occupy. Whether they find themselves on the winning or losing side of a conflict, those from warborne communities are likely to bear trauma for the rest of their lives, their sense of safety and mortality forever marred by the mass casualties and destruction of war.
Warborne are often strategic, devastated, determined, calculating, unwavering, and devoted.
features: Brave Face: Once per session when you would be forced to mark a Stress, you can **spend a Hope** instead.
